description: Gossip propagation flavor text. After a moral choice resolves and propagatesOnDay arrives, the world reacts through camp chatter, NPC greeting changes, and whispered reputation. The player never sees their score — only these reactions.

camp_chatter.description: Ambient lines overheard in camp after gossip propagates. Sorted by moral band at time of propagation.
very_positive: Did you hear? They gave their last medicine to that stranger's kid. The whole course.
The one from the eastern shelter — people say they buried every body they found on the ridge. Every one.
Someone told me they sat with old Mara all night. Didn't ask for anything. Just sat.
I heard they turned down a clean trade route to carry a wounded stranger back to camp. On their back.
The Peacekeepers are talking about them. Not the bad kind of talking.
Word is they gave seeds to the last farmer on the plateau. The whole stock. Their own stock.
They say even the raiders won't touch that one. Too much... weight, I guess. Too much weight behind the name.
A child in the east quarter drew a picture of them. Calls them 'the kind one.' Hangs it on the wall.
The Knowledge Keepers want to meet them. Not to ask — to give. That's new.
I don't trust saints. But this one keeps showing up, and keeps giving, and hasn't asked for a single thing back.
positive: They helped the Peacekeeper on the north road. Shared supplies, I heard. Not nothing.
People say they listened to old Gregor's war story. The whole thing. Even the ugly parts.
Word around camp — they comforted the widow by the east fire. Sat with her through the bad hours.
The merchant at the crossroads gives them a nod now. Fair trader, apparently.
I heard they buried a body near the water tower. Properly. Not just kicked dirt over it.
Someone said they gave food to that raider with the broken gun. The raider told them about the next raid.
The doctor at the clinic speaks well of them. Something about patience. About listening.
They stopped for the thirsty one on the desert road. Gave water. Got directions to a spring.
Not a saint. But decent. That's worth noting, these days.
slightly_positive: They helped someone on the road. I forget who. But they helped.
People say they're not bad. Which is... something.
The Peacekeepers don't frown when that name comes up. Low bar, but there it is.
I heard they gave a little food to a stranger. Not much. But they gave.
Someone said they listened to a story or two. Didn't mock anyone for telling one.
neutral: Who? Oh, them. I don't know. They come and go. Keep to themselves.
Never helped me. Never hurt me. That's the whole file on them.
The name doesn't ring any bells. Which is probably fine.
Neither the raiders nor the Peacekeepers mention them. That's a kind of safety.
Average. In the old world that was an insult. Now it's a blessing.
slightly_evil: Watch your gear around that one. I'm not saying they took anything. I'm saying watch it.
They walked past someone on the road. I saw it. Just walked past.
People say they refused a child. Could be rumor. Could be fact. The child remembers.
The merchant at the crossroads doesn't give them credit anymore. Something happened.
I don't like the look they give people who ask for help. The look says 'no' before the mouth does.
evil: Stay away from that one. I mean it. People who cross their path end up lighter.
They took from the injured man on the east road. Took his pack while he watched.
Word is they robbed the Knowledge Keeper. Ripped the notes right out of their hands.
The Peacekeepers have a description circulating. Matches that one pretty well.
A raider told me even their people talk about this one — and not with admiration. With caution.
Someone died on the south road. Didn't have to. This one walked past, pockets heavier than before.
The farmer's seed locker is empty. You know who did it. I know who did it. The fence knows.
Don't trade with them. The last person who did found their kit missing the next morning.
very_evil: Lock your shelter. That one is in the area.
The Peacekeepers posted a bounty. You know whose face is on it.
I watched them take from a dying woman. Her last bundle. While she tried to curse them.
The raiders respect them. Think about what that means. Think hard.
A child won't go near the east path anymore. Says 'the bad one' lives there.
They say you can trade with them — but only if you have something they can't just take.
The Knowledge Keepers tell their children about this one. As a warning.
Someone put a mark on the wall outside their shelter. A red mark. Everyone knows what it means.
The old man by the fire stopped telling stories. Says there's no point. Not with this one around.
Even the dogs cross the road when they see them coming. Animals know.

npc_greeting_shifts.description: How NPCs change their opening line when greeting the player after gossip propagates.
very_positive: Oh — you're the one they talk about. The kind one. What can I do for you?
I heard what you did for the family on the ridge. Thank you. Truly.
You don't have to buy anything. Sit. Eat. You've earned that much.
My daughter drew a picture of you. She's never met you. That's how far your name travels.
The Peacekeepers told us about you. We saved you a share. Here.
positive: Ah, you. I've heard good things. What do you need?
The merchant said you trade fair. That's enough for me. What can I offer?
You helped someone I know. So I'll help you. Fair's fair.
I trust you more than most. Which isn't saying much, but it's saying something.
slightly_positive: You seem alright. What are you after?
Haven't heard anything bad about you. That's practically a recommendation.
You can sit if you want. Fire's open.
neutral: I don't know you. State your business.
Sit if you want. Leave if you want. Makes no difference to me.
slightly_evil: Keep your distance. We can talk from here.
I know your face. I'll trade, but I'm watching my pack.
What do you want? Make it quick.
The children go inside when you come around. You notice that?
evil: You. I know what you did. Say your piece and go.
My hand's on my knife. Don't take it personally. Actually, do.
Last person who looked at me like that lost a tooth. State your business.
I'd spit, but you're not worth the moisture.
very_evil: Get away from my fire. Now.
I know your face. Everyone does. The bounty poster made sure of that.
You come any closer and I scream. The whole camp comes running.
I have nothing you can take. Leave.
The mark on my door is for you. You know what it means. Walk on.

whisper_lines.description: Lines murmured between NPCs when the player passes by. The player catches fragments.
very_positive: ...gave everything they had, I heard...
...the Peacekeepers want to meet them, not arrest them...
...buried every body on the ridge. Every single one...
...sat with the old woman all night. Didn't sleep...
...even the raiders won't...
...a saint, or the closest thing we have left...
positive: ...helped the doctor's patient. Didn't ask for pay...
...listened to old Gregor. The whole damn story...
...gave water to the one on the road...
evil: ...the Keeper screamed for an hour after...
very_evil: ...that's them. Don't look. Don't look...
...the bounty says alive, but I've heard 'dead' works too...
...even the raiders are careful around...
...took a child's toy from a grave. A grave...
...I won't sleep until they're gone from this camp...

gossip_decay.description: Gossip intensity fades over time. After 30 days without a new resolution, gossip downgrades one intensity level. After 60 days, it reaches baseline (neutral greetings). A single dramatic act resets the clock.
